newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's United Micro hires rival's ex-president.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's United Micro hires rival's ex-president.

text.p: Taiwan's No.2 chipmaker United Microelectronics Corp said on Wednesday it had given a senior post to Donald Brooks, who until April was president of market leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
Brooks was named a director on United Micro's board and given the post of president of international operations, company chairman Robert Tsao said at a news conference.
"We are fortunate to have someone of Mr Brooks' experience and background in the electronics industry actively involved in directing UMC's future," said Tsao.
Brooks would be responsible mainly for overseeing United Micro's relations with the U.S. semiconductor industry, including its own U.S. venture capital operations, Tsao said.
Brooks also will have a hand in formulating United Micro's overall business strategy, he said.
Brooks, an American, will be based in the United States.
The hiring of Brooks brought one of Taiwan's most conspicuous industrial rivalries to a new height.
Brooks left Taiwan Semiconductor in April, citing a desire to spend more time with his family in the United States, where he once was president of unlisted Fairchild Semiconductor.

Speculation about a job for him at United Micro began to swirl in mid-June when the company announced a T$500 billion (US$18 billion) plan to build six world-class wafer fabrication plants in southern Taiwan over 10 years.

When asked about Brooks at that time, Tsao pointedly declined to confirm or deny the rumours, telling reporters: "Whichever company can get the most talented people will stand out in the competition".

Within days after Brooks' leaving Taiwan Semiconductor, that company announced a T$400 billion, 10-year plan to build several advanced wafer fabs in a new high-tech park in southern Tainan -- the biggest investment in Taiwan to date.
It was less than three months later that United Micro unveiled its huge development scheme, bigger by T$100 billion but also to be based in the same Tainan science park.
In 1996, United Microelectronics reported a net profit of T$7.647 billion on sales of T$22.606 billion. It has set a 1997 net profit target of T$8.014 billion on sales of T$26.839 billion.
In 1996, Taiwan Semiconductor reported net profit of T$19.4 billion on sales of T$39.4 billion and has a 1997 net profit target of T$9.14 billion on sales of T$35.22 billion.
Independent electronic analyst Michael Hung estimated United Micro would have an earning per share of T$2.82 in 1997 before it goes ex-bonus issue in late July.
Taiwan Semiconductor would have earnings per share of T$3.92 after going ex-bonus issue in mid-June, Hung said.
